title: Sum of Remoteness of All Cells
statement:
`grid` is an `n x n` matrix whose cells are either blocked, holding `-1`, or open, holding a positive value. From an open cell you may step to an open cell directly above, below, left or right of it, and you may chain any number of such steps.

The remoteness of an open cell is the total of the values in all open cells that it **cannot** reach this way. A blocked cell has remoteness `0`.

Return the sum of the remoteness of every cell in `grid`.
notes:
## Intuition

Two open cells can reach each other exactly when they lie in the same connected region of open cells. So every cell in a region has the same remoteness: the grand total of all open values minus the region's own total. The brute force floods from every cell separately, which is O(n⁴); flooding each region once is enough.

## Approach

1. Scan the grid. Skip blocked cells and cells already `seen`.
2. Each unseen open cell starts a new region: push it on a `stack` and mark it `seen`.
3. Pop cells one by one (depth-first), adding the value to `sum` and counting `size`. Push every open, unseen neighbour inside the grid, marking it when it is pushed.
4. Store `[sum, size]` in `components` and add `sum` to `total`.
5. Each of a region's `size` cells misses exactly `total - sum`, so add `(total - sum) * size` for every region.

## Example 1, step by step

The open cells hold `1`, `5`, `4` and `3`, and they only touch diagonally, so each is a region of size 1. `components` becomes `[1, 1]`, `[5, 1]`, `[4, 1]`, `[3, 1]` and `total = 13`. The answer is `12 + 8 + 9 + 10 = 39`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): every cell is pushed and popped at most once and checks four neighbours.
- Space: O(n²) for `seen` and the stack.

## Pitfalls

- `total` is only known after the whole scan, so collect the regions first and combine them afterwards.
- Multiply by the region's `size`: every cell in it contributes its own remoteness.
- Blocked cells add nothing, and they also must not count toward any region.
- The answer can reach about 8·10^15 at the largest sizes, so Java and C need a 64-bit type.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | marks open cells already placed in a region |
| `components` | `[sum, size]` of each region |
| `total` | sum of every open cell's value |
| `stack` | cells of the current region waiting to be expanded |
| `sum`, `size` | value total and cell count of the current region |
| `nextRow`, `nextCol` | the neighbour being considered |
| `answer` | the sum of all remoteness values |

narration.8: Visit every cell in row-major order.
narration.10: Blocked cells and cells already in a region cannot start a new one.
narration.13: This open cell starts a new region; its total and cell count begin at zero.
narration.16: Mark the start cell when it is pushed so it is never pushed twice.
narration.17: Keep expanding until the region has no unexplored cells left.
narration.19: Every popped cell belongs to the region, so add its value.
narration.21: Look at the four neighbours of this cell.
narration.24: Skip neighbours that fall outside the grid.
narration.27: Skip walls and cells that are already part of a region.
narration.30: Mark the neighbour now so no other cell pushes it again.
narration.31: Push it so it gets expanded later.
narration.34: The region is complete: remember its total and size.
narration.35: Add the region to the grand total of all open values.
narration.40: Each region is visited once more, now that the grand total is known.
narration.41: Every one of its size cells misses exactly the values outside the region.
narration.43: The sum over all regions is the sum of every cell's remoteness.
